## Quarto

Quarto enables you to weave together content and executable code into a finished document. To learn more about Quarto see <https://quarto.org>.

## Running Code

When you click the **Render** button a document will be generated that includes both content and the output of embedded code. You can embed code like this:

```{r}
1 + 1
```

You can add options to executable code like this 

```{r}
#| echo: false
2 * 2
```

The `echo: false` option disables the printing of code (only output is displayed).

## Displaying code without rendering


```r
1+1
```

is not the same as 

```{r}
1 + 1
```

I can also do it in my markdown text where i know that 1+1=`{r} 1+1`.

## Rendering plots in quarto documents


```{r}
library(ggplot2)
```


```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "Petal width vs Petal Length in iris dataset"
iris |> ggplot(aes(x=Petal.Width,Petal.Length,col=Species)) + geom_point()
```

## Rendering table within quarto documents

```{r}
library(gt)
```

```{r}
iris |> gt() |>   tab_header(
    title = "Iris dataset from fisher & Anderson",
    subtitle = md("`iris` is an R dataset")
  ) |>   data_color(
    columns = Species,
    method = "factor",
    palette = "viridis"
  )
```

## Use a different output format

All formats: https://quarto.org/docs/output-formats/all-formats.html

```yaml
---
title: "My Document"
format: 
  pdf
---
```

or `quarto render quarto render Introduction/first_quarto_file/first_quarto_document.qmd --to pdf`
